resources.string: Only your contacts are offered: you must hold the person you add. On a board they need not hold the others — the roster reaches them with the board\'s key.
Everyone you know is already in this group.
Pick from your contacts. A group needs at least three people, you included — with two, you already have a conversation.
You can read, but not send: you don’t hold everyone here as a contact yet (%1$s). Trade cards with them, then you can join in.
Some copies have not landed yet — they will keep trying on their own.

Everyone must hold everyone as a contact — you can’t send until you do.

Anyone in the group can add anyone. Nobody can be removed, ever.

Someone added today sees nothing from before — there is no shared history to give them.

Messages can’t be forged: each one travels sealed, person to person, so nobody can write as anybody else.

Leaving only hides the group on your phone. The others keep it, and keep each other.

Everyone here reads and writes one shared board, so one message reaches everyone at once — you don’t need to hold everyone as a contact to send. Whoever adds someone must hold them; nobody else has to.

Anyone in the group can add anyone. Nobody can be removed, ever.

Someone added today sees the recent pages, not everything ever said.

Each message is signed by its sender’s key: nobody can write as anybody else, and what you write can be shown to be yours.

Leaving only hides the group on your phone. The others keep it, and keep each other.
Couldn’t reach %1$s — tap again to retry them.
Leave %1$s? It disappears from this device; the others keep talking without you, and a fresh invitation brings it back.
